memory_candidates.content: Candidate (d), the time-axis Ramsey-coloured summary, is Buchi's own 1962 proof of the complementation step inside the MSO-over-<Z,<> route: Thomas 1997 'Languages, Automata, and Logic' p. 30 states Buchi represents recognizable sets as finite unions U_i V_i^omega over classes of a finite-index segment congruence and applies a form of Ramsey's theorem; determinization (McNaughton/Safra) is the alternative proof. So Safra/Piterman, Safraless and Ramsey are three proofs of one step, not three routes, and no truth-value discrimination between the MSO frame and the Ramsey substrate exists on any fixture.

From FormalSystem.Metalogic.WeakCanonical.infinite_ramsey_pairs and a composition law (c i k = comp (c i j) (c j k) for i<j<k), an idempotent homogeneous colour follows in about eight lines: obtain the homogeneous g and tau, take hτ 0 1, hτ 1 2, hτ 0 2, rewrite h02 with the composition law and the first two. The backward mirror is the same proof on the colouring (i,j) |-> c (t - j) (t - i) with casts via exact_mod_cast; do not insert `simp only at` on the three hypotheses (they are already beta-reduced and simp reports no progress). Both compile on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

When lean_local_search returns index=unavailable, the evidence tier for 'absent from Mathlib' claims is a grep sweep over .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib. At pin v4.33.0-rc1: 'ramsey' hits only Combinatorics/Hindman.lean, Combinatorics/HalesJewett.lean and RingTheory false positives; no Buchi/parity/Rabin/Muller/omega-regular anywhere; Computability/ is finite-word only (DFA, NFA, EpsilonNFA, RegularExpressions, MyhillNerode, TuringMachine, Partrec). Literature FTS (literature-search.sh) can also return degraded=true with empty results; --toc still works and chunk files can be grepped/read directly.
